11.text: The transition from the first to the second class of keˊlet is quite gradual

12.text: and almost imperceptible. One shaman of the Reindeer people in the Telqäˊp

13.text: tundra told me that a few years before, when he was visiting at the secluded

14.text: house of a Keˊrek family,² a keˊlᴇ came at dusk to the dwelling, and called

15.text: from the outside for his wife to come out. He had evidently lost his way

16.text: and had mistaken this for his own house. He went on to tell his supposed

17.text: wife that he had caught all the fish in the nearest two rivers, and he flung

18.text: down his load with such force that the ground trembled. Then he thrust a

19.text: pair of boots made of stone into the sleeping-room, and asked for dry shoes.

20.text: When he tried to creep into the sleeping-room, the inmates poured the

21.text: contents of the chamber-vessel on his head, and he immediately fled, gibbering

22.text: away at a furious rate. The fish remained behind, and afforded sufficient

23.text: food for all the people of the near-by villages for half a year. It will be

24.text: seen that this keˊlᴇ is described as an unfriendly spirit and at the same time

25.text: as an earthly being living by catching real fish.

26.text: Another story relates that a keˊlᴇ tribe lived somewhere on the Arctic

27.text: shore. The Chukchee led a war of extermination against them, and at last

28.text: the “spirits,” unable to continue the strife, made themselves invisible.

29.text: I have already spoken of the tradition according to which several human

30.text: tribes are supposed to have emigrated in ancient times from the Chukchee

31.text: country.³ These tribes correspond to the Eskimo tornit (pl. of tuneq).⁴

32.text: Cannibal giants similar to those of the Chukchee appear also in Eskimo tales.

33.text: The tribes which emigrated are supposed to have been of ordinary stature.

34.text: The Chukchee also believe in the existence of a race of giants, who,

35.text: unlike the keˊlet, do not harm men. They are called loˊlg̣ɪlɪt. The tales

36.text: about them are somewhat similar to those found among the Eskimo. The

37.text: giants are said to live on the other shore of the sea, inside of large tent-like

38.text: mountains. When they make a fire, the smoke escapes through the opening

39.text: on the top of the mountains.
